materiality: Shared FlashAttention and SageAttention varlen preparation could fail under torch.compile with dynamic shapes because Inductor rewrites cumsum-of-symbolic-constant lengths into an unsupported FakeTensor/Node multiplication, while the no-mask path also forced a GPU-to-CPU .item() graph break.

The successor replaces uniform-length cumsum construction with arange, removes the no-mask .item() path, adds explicit zero-length offset handling and an upstream dynamic compile regression, making this a shared compiled-attention execution boundary rather than a cosmetic optimization.
disconfirmingEvidence: Upstream reports exact eager parity and successful dynamic fullgraph compilation for real flash-attn 2.8.3 on one H200, but that is an upstream measurement and not an SZL runtime receipt.

The masked key-length path remains data-dependent and retains a necessary .item(); upstream verification cited the real FlashAttention backend, not independent SageAttention hardware/runtime closure, and the self-review notes no direct CPU unit test for the helpers.

boundedResources.sourceFixtures: CPU/helper shape arithmetic plus existing source CI; no checkpoint or model download is required
boundedResources.acceleratorClosure: one bounded existing-owner run only on already available hardware/backends actually consumed by SZL; no paid job is authorized
boundedResources.weights: use only an already-admitted local fixture or tiny synthetic attention harness unless a separately governed exact checkpoint is already available; do not mirror weights for this wave

requiredEvidence: Bind exact Diffusers commit/wheel or image, Torch/Inductor, Python, attention backend and kernel package identities; bind exact model/checkpoint only if a full pipeline is actually exercised.

Preserve the immediate predecessor or equivalent known-bad dynamic-shape fixture that reproduces the symbolic cumsum failure and the no-mask graph-break behavior; include zero-length, batch-one, changing batch, changing sequence and masked/unmasked controls.

Require helper offset and max-length equality against an independent reference across the declared dynamic-shape matrix, including zero-length sequences and malformed/inconsistent masks that must fail explicitly rather than silently reshape.

For every backend SZL actually consumes, compare eager versus compiled outputs under fixed inputs and declared tolerances; FlashAttention evidence does not automatically qualify SageAttention, and source tests do not qualify an unavailable accelerator backend.

Exercise compile cache warm/cold behavior, shape changes, cancellation/error propagation and restart where the owning runtime supports them; retain raw compiler/runtime failures and do not convert graph breaks into PASS.
Preserve eager/uncompiled attention or the previously qualified backend as rollback, and do not change a production compile/backend default until exact owner-level evidence passes.
